text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will make a lightning visit to the Vatican today to sign an agreement with the Holy See settling relations between the Hungarian state and the Catholic Church.
- A senior Calvinist Church official yesterday expressed major reservations regarding several details of the Hungarian-Vatican agreement to be signed today.
- The cabinet agreed yesterday to submit 57 bills to Parliament in the second half, with priority going to the state and social insurance budgets, related tax bills, and agriculture.
- The Free Democrat parliamentary group will hold a two-day meeting, starting today, to consider the 1998 budget and legislative tasks ahead in the second half of the year.
- Zsolt Semjen, a candidate for the Christian Democrat presidency, said Thursday he favors integration and is thus against expelling anybody.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs expressed satisfaction that the shortcomings of the EU summit in Amsterdam will not slow down the process of enlargement, according to Thursday's Financial Times.
- Hungary and Slovenia agreed Thursday that the proposed M70 highway will cross the common border at Tornyiszentmiklos and a Slovene border station will be established at the village of Pince.
- AES Corp., the American owner of the Tisza power plant Tiszai Eromu, plans to spend more than $1 billion on developments.
- The price of Antenna Hungaria shares has doubled in the past month in over-the-counter trading.
- Truck traffic came to a standstill on the Hungary-Slovenia border Thursday in a protest by Slovene truck drivers.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Ministry of Finance intends to reduce the expected social insurance fund deficit by nearly Ft 25 billion this year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The Washington Post, in a report on Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, Thursday queried how the three countries most likely to join NATO will be able to raise funds for procuring fighter planes.
- The state railway MAV needs to be reorganized to control a debt spiral which could reach Ft 21-24 billion by year's end, managing director Istvan Sipos said yesterday.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The deadline for applicants to submit compensation claims to the Hungarian Jewish Heritage Public Foundation has been extended by two weeks due to continuing demand.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- A total of 1 million ordinary shares of the pharmaceutical company Human Rt. will be introduced onto the Budapest Stock Exchange today.
